179	
180	\section{Where Clauses}
181	\seclabel{where-clauses}
182	
183	\note{The \KWD{where} clause syntax in this section is out of date.}
184	
185	\begin{Grammar}
186	\emph{Where} &::=& \KWD{where} \{ \emph{WhereClauseList} \}\\
187	\emph{WhereClauseList} &::=& \emph{WhereClause}(\EXP{,}
188	\emph{WhereClause})$^*$ \\
189	\emph{WhereClause} &::=& \emph{Id} \emph{Extends}\\
190	&$|$& \emph{TypeAlias} \\
191	&$|$& \emph{NatConstraint} \\
192	&$|$& \emph{IntConstraint} \\
193	&$|$& \emph{BoolConstraint} \\
194	&$|$& \emph{UnitConstraint} \\
195	&$|$& \emph{TypeRef} \KWD{coerces} \emph{TypeRef}\\
196	&$|$& \emph{TypeRef} \KWD{widens} \emph{TypeRef}\\
197	\end{Grammar}
198	
199	
200	Static parameters may have constraints placed on them
201	in a \KWD{where} clause.
202	A \KWD{where} clause begins with
203	\KWD{where}, followed by a sequence of static
204	parameter constraints enclosed in braces \EXP{\{} and \EXP{\}},
205	and separated by commas.
206	
207	
208	A \KWD{where} clause may introduce new static variables, i.e., identifiers
209	for types and other static entities that may not be static parameters.
210	We use the term \emph{\KWD{where}-clause variables} to refer to
211	static variables that are not also static parameters.
212	The \KWD{where}-clause variables must be bound in a \KWD{where} clause.
213	
214	
215	A static parameter constraint is one of the following forms:
216	\begin{itemize}
217	\item a trait constraint consisting of the identifier of
218	a naked type variable, followed by \KWD{extends}
219	followed by a set of trait references which may include naked type variables,
220	\item a type alias (described in \secref{type-alias}),
221	\item an arithmetic constraint,
222	\item a boolean constraint,
223	\item a unit equality constraint,
224	\item a \KWD{coerces} constraint (described in
225	  \secref{coercion-declarations}), or
226	\item a \KWD{widens} constraint (described in
227	  \secref{coercion-declarations}).
228	\end{itemize}
229	A \KWD{where} clause may include mutually recursive constraints.
230	All static variables in a trait, object, or functional declaration must
231	occur either as a static parameter or as a \KWD{where}-clause variable.
232	\appref{where-calculus} describes a Fortress core calculus with
233	\KWD{where} clauses.
234	
235	A \KWD{where}-clause variable may not appear as a static argument
236	in an \KWD{extends} clause.
237	Such an occurrence would make the declared trait or object a subtype of
238	one instantiation for each type that the variable may stand for,
239	which instantiation exclusion forbids
240	(\secref{trait-types} and \secref{trait-decls});
241	the second of the three declarations below shows why.
242	\revision{revival-where}{This restriction is new.
243	The three declarations that follow were offered as legal by the
244	Working Draft of February 2011; they are kept as examples of what is not
245	allowed, each with the way to write it.}
246	
247	In particular, a trait declaration may not extend other instantiations
248	of itself through a \KWD{where}-clause variable.
249	The following declaration would express that the static parameter \VAR{S}
250	of \VAR{C} is covariant, making \EXP{C\llbracket{}S\rrbracket} a subtype of
251	\EXP{C\llbracket{}T\rrbracket} for every supertype \VAR{T} of \VAR{S};
252	it is not allowed:
253	%(* Not allowed! *)
254	%trait C[\S\] extends C[\T\]
255	%  where {S extends T, T extends Object}
256	%end
257	\begin{Fortress}
258	\(\mathtt{(*}\;\hbox{\rm  Not allowed! \unskip}\;\mathtt{*)}\)\\
259	\(\KWD{trait} C\llbracket{}S\rrbracket \KWD{extends} C\llbracket{}T\rrbracket\)\\
260	{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \KWD{where} \{S \KWD{extends} T, T \KWD{extends} \TYP{Object}\}\)\-\\\poptabs
261	\(\KWD{end}\)
262	\end{Fortress}
263	Static parameters are invariant:
264	\EXP{C\llbracket{}S\rrbracket} is a subtype of \EXP{C\llbracket{}T\rrbracket}
265	only if \VAR{S} and \VAR{T} are the same type.
266	A value of one instantiation is widened to another by a function
267	whose bounded static parameters state that one argument extends the other:
268	%trait C[\S\]
269	%  getter item(): S
270	%end
271	%object CItem[\S\](item: S) extends C[\S\] end
272	%widen[\T, S extends T\](c: C[\S\]): C[\T\] = CItem[\T\](c.item)
273	\begin{Fortress}
274	\(\KWD{trait}\:C\llbracket{}S\rrbracket\)\\
275	{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \KWD{getter}\:\VAR{item}()\COLON S\)\-\\\poptabs
276	\(\KWD{end}\)\\
277	\(\KWD{object}\:\TYP{CItem}\llbracket{}S\rrbracket(\VAR{item}\COLON S) \KWD{extends}\:C\llbracket{}S\rrbracket \KWD{end}\)\\
278	\(\VAR{widen}\llbracket{}T, S \KWD{extends}\:T\rrbracket(c\COLON C\llbracket{}S\rrbracket)\COLON C\llbracket{}T\rrbracket = \TYP{CItem}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket(c.\VAR{item})\)
279	\end{Fortress}
280	so that, where a trait \TYP{Dog} extends a trait \TYP{Animal} and \VAR{d}
281	is a \EXP{C\llbracket\TYP{Dog}\rrbracket},
282	\EXP{\VAR{widen}\llbracket\TYP{Animal}, \TYP{Dog}\rrbracket(d)} is a
283	\EXP{C\llbracket\TYP{Animal}\rrbracket} with the same item.
284	The library's covariant collections are written this way.
285	\revision{revival-covariance}{The Working Draft of February 2011 said that
286	trait declarations are allowed to extend other instantiations of themselves,
287	and gave the declaration above as the way to express covariance.
288	The type group's later design declares variance instead with a
289	\KWD{covariant} modifier on a static parameter
290	(the team's later Types chapter, Luchangco, 2012),
291	which is implemented on neither the interpreter nor the compiled path;
292	the revival's decision record and row~404 of its gap ledger
293	say what is known of it.}
294	
295	
296	Trait declarations need not have any static parameters in order
297	to have a \KWD{where} clause. But the following trait
298	declaration is not allowed:
299	%(* Not allowed! *)
300	%trait C extends D[\T\]
301	%  where {T extends Object}
302	%end
303	\begin{Fortress}
304	\(\mathtt{(*}\;\hbox{\rm  Not allowed! \unskip}\;\mathtt{*)}\)\\
305	\(\KWD{trait} C \KWD{extends} D\llbracket{}T\rrbracket\)\\
306	{\tt~~}\pushtabs\=\+\(  \KWD{where} \{T \KWD{extends} \TYP{Object}\}\)\-\\\poptabs
307	\(\KWD{end}\)
308	\end{Fortress}
309	In this declaration, trait \VAR{C} would be a subtrait of \emph{every}
310	instantiation of parametric trait \VAR{D}. Thus, trait \VAR{C} would have all
311	of the methods of every instantiation of \VAR{D}. By thinking of the
312	declaration this way, we can see what restrictions we need to impose on
313	the trait \VAR{C} in order for it to be sensible. If trait
314	\VAR{C} inherits a method declaration that refers to \VAR{T}, it really
315	contains infinitely many methods (one for each instantiation of \VAR{T}).
316	However, instantiations of the \KWD{where}-clause variables are not
317	explicit from the program text as static parameters are.
318	It must be possible to infer which method is referred to at the call site.
319	%%So every method invocation is annotated with static types by type inference.
320	If there is not enough information to infer which method is called,
321	type checking rejects the
322	program and requires more type information from the programmer.
323	Programmers always can provide more type information by using type
324	ascription as described in \secref{type-ascription}.
325	But trait \VAR{C} would also be a subtype of every pair of
326	different instantiations of \VAR{D},
327	which exclude each other by instantiation exclusion,
328	so no such restriction makes the declaration sensible:
329	that is why it is not allowed.
330	\revision{revival-every}{The Working Draft of February 2011 said that this
331	declaration is legal. The paragraph above, the team's own account of why
332	such a trait is dangerous, is kept as the reason for the restriction stated
333	at the start of this section.}

59	amendment of 9~October 2026.

62	the traits that immediately extend the declared trait and that they must
63	explicitly extend it, is replaced by normative text: every listed type
64	extends the declared trait \VAR{T}, and every value of type \VAR{T} is a
65	value of one of the listed types; a listed type may be an instantiation of
66	a parameterized trait whose static arguments contain no static variable
67	other than the static parameters of \VAR{T}; and a trait or object that explicitly extends
68	\VAR{T} is a subtype of a listed type, or a trait with a \KWD{comprises}
69	clause of its own each of whose listed types meets the same requirement, or
70	a trait with static parameters that at least one trait or object extends
71	and every trait or object extending it is a subtype of a listed type.

73	kept in its note, and the example of \TYP{Molecule} is unchanged.

75	on trait identifiers earlier in the section, whether an instantiation of a
76	parameterized trait may be listed: it may.

78	contain a \KWD{where}-clause variable of the declaration of \VAR{T} as well,

88	clause as coverage: the clause ``specifies a set of types and generic types

985	  // The k-th inference variable that a walk of a question meets, renamed apart. Its hash is its
986	  // number, so a renaming asks the JVM for no identity hash.
987	  private final class Renamed(val k: Int) {
988	    override def toString = "renamed" + k
989	    override def hashCode = k
990	  }
991	  private val renamed = new java.util.ArrayList[_InferenceVarType]()
992	  private def renamedVar(k: Int): _InferenceVarType = renamed.synchronized {
993	    while (renamed.size <= k) renamed.add(NF.make_InferenceVarType(typeSpan, false, new Renamed(renamed.size)))
994	    renamed.get(k)
995	  }
996	
997	  /** The two types with their type inference variables renamed apart, each in the order that a
998	   *  walk of x and then y meets it; None if they hold an inference variable of another kind. */
999	  def renamedApart(x: Type, y: Type): Option[(Type, Type)] = {
1000	    val names = new java.util.HashMap[_InferenceVarType, _InferenceVarType]()
1001	    var other = false
1002	    object renamer extends Walker {
1003	      override def walk(n: Any): Any = n match {
1004	        case v: _InferenceVarType =>
1005	          val r = names.get(v)
1006	          if (r != null) r else { val fresh = renamedVar(names.size); names.put(v, fresh); fresh }
1007	        case _: _InferenceVarInt => other = true; n
1008	        case _: _InferenceVarOp => other = true; n
1009	        case _ => super.walk(n)
1010	      }
1011	    }
1012	    val rx = renamer(x).asInstanceOf[Type]
1013	    val ry = renamer(y).asInstanceOf[Type]
1014	    if (other) None else Some((rx, ry))
1015	  }
1016	}

22	/**
23	 * Represents a list of variable name to static parameter bindings for some
24	 * context. All instances of this class should be created with `KindEnv.makeFresh`
25	 * or with the `extend` method.
26	 */
27	abstract sealed class KindEnv extends StaticEnv[StaticParam] {
28	
29	  /** My type. */
30	  type Env = KindEnv
31	
32	  /** My binding type. */
33	  type EnvBinding = KindBinding
34	
35	  /** Extend me with the immediate bindings of the given node. */
36	  def extend(node: Node): KindEnv =
37	    new NestedKindEnv(this, KindEnv.extractNodeBindings(node))
38	
39	  /** Extend me with the immediate bindings of the given nodes. */
40	  def extend[T <: Node](nodes: Iterable[T]): KindEnv =
41	    new NestedKindEnv(this, nodes.flatMap(KindEnv.extractNodeBindings))
42	
43	  /** Extend me with the immediate bindings of the given node. */
44	  def extend(node: Node, where: Option[WhereClause]): KindEnv = {
45	    val whereBindings = where.map(KindEnv.extractNodeBindings)
46	                             .getOrElse(Iterable.empty)
47	    val nodeBindings = KindEnv.extractNodeBindings(node)
48	    new NestedKindEnv(this, whereBindings ++ nodeBindings)
49	  }
50	
51	  /** Extend me with the immediate bindings of the given nodes. */
52	  def extend[T<:Node](nodes: Iterable[T], where: Option[WhereClause]): KindEnv = {
53	    val whereBindings = where.map(KindEnv.extractNodeBindings)
54	                             .getOrElse(Iterable.empty)
55	    val nodesBindings = nodes.flatMap(KindEnv.extractNodeBindings)
56	    new NestedKindEnv(this, whereBindings ++ nodesBindings)
57	  }
58	
59	  /**
60	   * Get the type of the given variable name, if it is bound. The resulting
61	   * type will only be defined if this name maps to a bool, int, or nat static
62	   * parameter.
63	   */
64	  def getType(x: Name): Option[Type] = lookup(x).flatMap(b =>
65	    b.sparam.getKind match {
66	      case _:KindBool => Some(Types.BOOLEAN)
67	      case _:KindInt => Some(Types.INT_LITERAL)
68	      case _:KindNat => Some(Types.INT_LITERAL)
69	      case _ => None
70	    })
71	
72	  def staticParam(x: Name): Option[StaticParam] = lookup(x).map(_.sparam)
73	}
74	
75	/** The single empty kind environment. */
76	protected object EmptyKindEnv extends KindEnv with EmptyStaticEnv[StaticParam] {
77	}
78	
79	/**
80	 * A kind environment with a parent and some explicit bindings.
81	 *
82	 * @param parent A kind environment that this one extends.
83	 * @param _bindings A collection of all the bindings in this environment.
84	 */
85	class NestedKindEnv (protected val parent: KindEnv,
86	                               _bindings: Iterable[KindBinding])
87	    extends KindEnv with NestedStaticEnv[StaticParam] {
88	
89	  /** Internal representation of `bindings` is a map. */
90	  val bindings: Map[Name, KindBinding] =
91	    Map(_bindings.map(b => (b.name, b)).toSeq:_*)
92	}

94	/** Companion module for KindEnv; contains "static" members. */
95	object KindEnv extends StaticEnvCompanion[StaticParam] {
96	
97	  /** My type. */
98	  type Env = KindEnv
99	
100	  /** My binding type. */
101	  type EnvBinding = KindBinding
102	
103	  /** Creates a fresh kind environment. */
104	  def makeFresh: KindEnv = EmptyKindEnv.extend(Nil)
105	
106	  /** Extract out the bindings in node. */
107	  protected def extractNodeBindings(node: Node) : Iterable[KindBinding] =
108	    node match {
109	      // Trivially add this param.
110	      case p:StaticParam => Iterable(KindBinding(p.getName, p))
111	      
112	      // Extract bindings from generic declaration.
113	      case g:Generic =>
114	        toListFromImmutable(g.getHeader.getStaticParams)
115	          .map(p => KindBinding(p.getName, p))
116	      
117	      // Extract where clause bindings.
118	      case SWhereClause(info, bindings, _) => bindings.map {
119	        
120	        // If a type binding, create a new TypeParam.
121	        case b:WhereBinding if b.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindType] =>
122	          val sp = NF.makeTypeParam(info.getSpan, b.getName, b.getSupers, none[Type], false)
123	          KindBinding(b.getName, sp)
124	
125	        // A nat or int binding is a size, as a nat or int static parameter is.
126	        case b:WhereBinding if b.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindNat] || b.getKind.isInstanceOf[KindInt] =>
127	          val sp = NF.makeStaticParam(info.getSpan, null, b.getName,
128	                                      java.util.Collections.emptyList[BaseType],
129	                                      java.util.Collections.emptyList[BaseType],
130	                                      none[Type], false, b.getKind)
131	          KindBinding(b.getName, sp)
132	
133	        // Other kinds not supported yet.
134	        case _ => NI.nyi("non-type where clause bindings")
135	      }
136	      
137	      case _ => Iterable.empty
138	    }
139	}

=== OpenTypeChecker.test
tests=OpenTypeChecker
typecheck
=== OpenTypeChecker.fss
(* A value whose trait lists Box[\E\] where [\E\] opens, at a call, to a Box at a type of its own, and packs back into the trait. *)
component OpenTypeChecker
export Executable

trait AnyBox comprises { Box[\E\] } where [\E extends Object\]
end
object Box[\E\](item: E) extends AnyBox end

mk(): AnyBox = Box[\ZZ32\](3)
same[\E\](b: Box[\E\]): Box[\E\] = b
count[\E\](b: Box[\E\]): ZZ32 = 1

run(): () = do
    a: AnyBox = same(mk())
    k: ZZ32 = count(mk())
    println(k)
  end

end
=== XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker.test
tests=XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker
compile
compile_err_contains=File XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker.fss has 2 errors.
=== XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker.fss
(* An opened type equals only itself: it does not reach a declared type that names another type, in a result or a variable. *)
component XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker
export Executable

trait AnyBox comprises { Box[\E\] } where [\E extends Object\]
end
object Box[\E\](item: E) extends AnyBox end

mk(): AnyBox = Box[\ZZ32\](3)
same[\E\](b: Box[\E\]): Box[\E\] = b
get[\E\](b: Box[\E\]): E = b.item
asInt(b: AnyBox): ZZ32 = get(b)

run(): () = do
    y: Box[\ZZ32\] = same(mk())
    println(asInt(mk()))
  end

end
=== XXXOpenTypeTwoChecker.test
tests=XXXOpenTypeTwoChecker
compile
compile_err_contains=File XXXOpenTypeTwoChecker.fss has 1 error.
=== XXXOpenTypeTwoChecker.fss
(* Two values opened in one call have two types, not one. *)
component XXXOpenTypeTwoChecker
export Executable

trait AnyBox comprises { Box[\E\] } where [\E extends Object\]
end
object Box[\E\](item: E) extends AnyBox end

mk(): AnyBox = Box[\ZZ32\](3)
two[\E\](a: Box[\E\], b: Box[\E\]): ZZ32 = 2

run(): () = println(two(mk(), mk()))

end
=== XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker.test
tests=XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker
compile
compile_err_contains=File XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker.fss has 1 error.
compile_err_WIcontains=Could not check call to function upcast
=== XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker.fss
(* The shape of Amin and Tate's 2016 unsoundness: a value whose trait lists Constrain[\A,T,B\] for some B with T extends B and B extends A would be evidence that T is an A; the opened B has only its binding's bound, so the call is refused. *)
component XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker
export Executable

trait Witness[\A, T\] comprises { Constrain[\A, T, B\] } where [\B extends A\] { T extends B }
end
trait Constrain[\A, T, B extends A\] extends Witness[\A, T\] end

upcast[\A, T, B extends A\](c: Constrain[\A, T, B\], b: B): A = b
convert[\T, U\](t: T, w: Witness[\U, T\]): U = upcast(w, t)

run(): () = println("unreachable")

end

(* A trait may list Nt[\n\] where [\nat n\]: an Nt at every size extends it, and a call opens the value to its own size. *)
component NatOpenWalk
export Executable

trait NatParamT comprises { Nt[\n\] } where [\nat n\]
  getter toZZ(): ZZ32
end
value object Nt[\nat n\] extends NatParamT
  getter toZZ(): ZZ32 = n
end

mk(z: ZZ32): NatParamT = if z = 0 then Nt[\0\] else Nt[\3\] end
size[\nat n\](x: Nt[\n\]): ZZ32 = n

run(): () = do
    assert(size(mk(3)), 3, "trait-parameters.tex, section \"Nat and Int Parameters\": a value opened to its own size")
    assert(size(mk(0)), 0, "trait-parameters.tex, section \"Nat and Int Parameters\": a value opened to its own size")
    r = typecase mk(0) of
          Nt[\0\] => "zero"
          else => "other"
        end
    assert(r, "zero", "internal-document.tex, subsection \"Overloaded operators\": a size name is not known to differ from a numeral")
    assert(mk(3).toZZ, 3, "a listed type at a size the clause names by a where-clause variable")
  end

end

(* A value whose trait lists Nt[\n\] where [\nat n\] opens, at a call, to an Nt at its own size. *)
component NatOpenChecker
export Executable

trait NatParamT comprises { Nt[\n\] } where [\nat n\]
end
value object Nt[\nat n\] extends NatParamT end

trait Sized end
object Store[\nat n\](v: ZZ32) extends Sized end

mk(): NatParamT = Nt[\3\]
size[\nat n\](x: Nt[\n\]): ZZ32 = n
take[\nat n\](x: Nt[\n\]): Store[\n\] = Store[\n\](n)
sizePlus[\nat n\](x: Nt[\n\], i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = n + i

run(): () = do
    z: ZZ32 = size(mk())
    s: Sized = take(mk())
    w: ZZ32 = sizePlus(mk(), 1)
    r: String = typecase mk() of
        Nt[\0\] => "zero"
        else => "other"
      end
    println(z)
    println(w)
    println(r)
  end

end

(** %List%.  We return a %Generator% for non-list-specific operations
    for which reuse of the %Generator% will not increase asymptotic
    complexity, but return a %List% in cases (such as %map% and
    %filter%) where it will.  Indexing on lists operates from the
    left, and ordering is lexicographic reading from the left. *)
trait List[\E\] extends { AnyList, LexicographicOrder[\List[\E\],E\] }
        excludes { Number, HasRank, String }
  (** %left% and %extractLeft% return the leftmost element in the list
      (and in the latter case, the remainder of the list without its
      leftmost element).  They return %Nothing% if the list is empty.
      %right% and %extractRight% do the same with the rightmost
      element. *)

  getter right():Maybe[\E\]

    (** %concatMap% is an in-place version of the %nest% method from

usage: ledger.py [-h] COMMAND ...

The gap ledger's tool: it owns the ledger's format, reads its rows, and is
the only way to write them.

positional arguments:
  COMMAND

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

usage: ledger.py COMMAND [ARGS] [--root DIR] [--ledger FILE] [--history FILE]

  heads                      one tab-separated line per row: number, status,
                             class, the claim's first 150 characters, and the
                             paths the row cites in backticks
  sections                   each section that holds a row table: its row
                             count and title, tab-separated
  section TITLE              the heads of that section's rows
  show N [--short]           row N under its section and table header; with
                             --short, its status, class, claim and the notes'
                             first 300 characters
  find WORDS [--open] [--cites FILE[:LINE]] [--all]
                             one line per row that holds every word (whole
                             words, or a word's start with a trailing *):
                             number, status, class, the claim's start; --open
                             leaves out FIXED, DUPLICATE and RETIRED; --cites
                             keeps the rows citing FILE (at LINE) and prints
                             the lines they cite; at most 10 rows unless --all
  count                      the rows by status, kind and area; nothing stored

If a trait \VAR{T} excludes a trait \VAR{U},
the two traits are mutually exclusive:
neither can extend the other, and no trait can extend them both.
As discussed in \secref{type-relations},
the exclusion relation is symmetric.
Thus, if \VAR{T} excludes \VAR{U}
then \VAR{U} excludes \VAR{T}
whether or not \VAR{T} is listed in an \KWD{excludes} clause
in the declaration of \VAR{U}.

If a trait declaration of \VAR{T} includes a \KWD{comprises} clause
then every type listed in its \KWD{comprises} clause extends \VAR{T},
and every value of type \VAR{T} is a value of one of the listed types.
A listed type may be an instantiation of a parameterized trait,
provided that every static variable that occurs in its static arguments
is a static parameter of \VAR{T}
or a \KWD{where}-clause variable of the declaration of \VAR{T}
(\secref{where-clauses}),
which the listed type then holds at every value of:
a trait declared
\EXP{\KWD{trait}\;\TYP{NatParam}\;\KWD{comprises}\;\{N\llbracket{}n\rrbracket\}\;\KWD{where}\;\llbracket\KWD{nat}\;n\rrbracket}
lists \EXP{N\llbracket{}n\rrbracket} at every \KWD{nat} value of \VAR{n}.
A trait or object that explicitly extends \VAR{T}
must be a subtype of a listed type,
unless it is a trait with a \KWD{comprises} clause of its own
each of whose listed types meets this requirement,
or a trait with static parameters
such that at least one trait or object extends it
and every trait or object that extends it
is a subtype of a listed type.
If \VAR{T} has static parameters,
these statements hold of each instantiation of \VAR{T},
with the static parameters of \VAR{T} in the listed types
replaced by the corresponding static arguments.
\revision{revival-comprises}{The Working Draft of February 2011 said here,
in a draft note, that the traits listed in a \KWD{comprises} clause
are exactly the traits that immediately extend \VAR{T}
and that each of them must list \VAR{T} in its \KWD{extends} clause.
The revival states the reading of the team's later Types chapter
(Luchangco, 2012) and of the type group's calculus Welterweight Fortress (2012):
the clause says to which types the values of \VAR{T} belong.
A parameterized trait with a static parameter that \VAR{T} does not have
can be listed only at particular static arguments;
it may stand unlisted between \VAR{T} and the listed types,
adding no value outside them,
when at least one trait or object extends it
and every one that does is a subtype of a listed type.
This also answers the third question of the draft note on trait identifiers above,
whether an instantiation of a parameterized trait may be listed: it may.
A \KWD{where}-clause variable of the declaration of \VAR{T} may also occur in a
listed type, as in the clause of the trait \TYP{NatParam} of \library,
which the team wrote as a comment and the revival restores.}
\note{
If the \KWD{comprises} clause of a trait \VAR{T} includes ``\EXP{\ldots}''
(and must therefore be in an API),
then in a component exporting the enclosing API,
other traits may explicitly extend \VAR{T},
but these traits may not be declared or imported by the API
(see \secref{apis}).}

A trait declaration of \VAR{T} that has no \KWD{comprises} clause,
or one that lists no type but ``\EXP{\ldots}'', may have a \emph{self-type parameter}:
a static parameter \VAR{X} of \VAR{T}
whose bounds include \VAR{T} at its own static parameters,
as in \EXP{\KWD{trait}\;T\llbracket{}X \KWD{extends} T\llbracket{}X\rrbracket\rrbracket},
or include an instantiation of a trait with a self-type parameter
that \VAR{T} also lists in its \KWD{extends} clause,
with \VAR{X} as the static argument for that self-type parameter.
In the bodies of the methods of \VAR{T},
\KWD{self} then has the type \EXP{T \cap X} (\secref{idn-ref}).
A trait or object declaration, or an object expression,
that extends an instantiation of \VAR{T}
must be a subtype of the static argument of that instantiation
for the self-type parameter of \VAR{T}; for a trait declaration the requirement is on
the type of \KWD{self} in the bodies of its methods (\secref{idn-ref}), the intersection of its type
with the types its \KWD{comprises} clause lists, or with its own self-type parameter \VAR{Y}.
An \KWD{int} parameter consists of
\KWD{int} followed by an identifier.
These parameters are instantiated at runtime with numeric values.
A \KWD{nat} parameter may be used to instantiate other
\KWD{nat} parameters, or to appear in any context that a
variable of type \EXP{\mathbb{N}32} can appear,
except that it cannot be assigned to.
An \KWD{int} parameter may be used to instantiate other
\KWD{int} parameters, or to appear in any context that a
variable of type \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} can appear,
except that it cannot be assigned to.
An argument whose type is a trait whose \KWD{comprises} clause lists a type at a
\KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} \KWD{where}-clause variable (\secref{trait-decls}),
passed where that listed type is expected
with a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int} parameter in the variable's place,
instantiates that parameter, for that call, with the size of the value itself,
a size known to equal only itself:
where
\EXP{\KWD{trait}\;\TYP{NatParam}\;\KWD{comprises}\;\{N\llbracket{}n\rrbracket\}\;\KWD{where}\;\llbracket\KWD{nat}\;n\rrbracket}
is declared, a \TYP{NatParam} passed to
\EXP{f\llbracket\KWD{nat}\;m\rrbracket(x\COLON N\llbracket{}m\rrbracket)}
instantiates \VAR{m} with the size of the \VAR{N} that it is.
\revision{revival-comprises}{The Working Draft of February 2011 did not say how
a size known only at run time reaches a \KWD{nat} parameter.
The sentence above states the rule of the team's comment on the trait
\TYP{NatParam} of \library: ``within that function n becomes a static nat
parameter''.}

(* A trait may list Box[\E\] where [\E\]: a Box at every type extends it, and a value of the trait is a Box at a type of its own. *)
component OpenTypeWalk
export Executable

trait AnyBox comprises { Box[\E\] } where [\E\]
  getter label(): String
end
object Box[\E\](item: E) extends AnyBox
  getter label(): String = "box"
end

mk(z: ZZ32): AnyBox = if z = 0 then Box[\ZZ32\](3) else Box[\String\]("s") end
item[\E\](b: Box[\E\]): E = b.item

run(): () = do
    assert(item(mk(0)), 3, "traits.tex, section \"Trait Declarations\": a value of the trait is a value of a listed type")
    assert(item(mk(1)), "s", "traits.tex, section \"Trait Declarations\": a value of the trait is a value of a listed type")
    r = typecase mk(1) of
          Box[\ZZ32\] => "ZZ32"
          Box[\String\] => "String"
          else => "other"
        end
    assert(r, "String", "traits.tex, section \"Trait Declarations\": the listed type at the value's own type")
    assert(mk(0).label, "box", "a member of the trait")
  end

end

1	# Committing and pushing
2	
3	**scratch**
4	: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.
5	
6	Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.
7	
8	## What to commit
9	
10	- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
11	- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
12	- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
13	- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
14	- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
15	- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
16	- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.
17	
18	## How to commit
19	
20	Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:
21	
22	    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>
23	
24	- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
25	- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
26	- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
27	- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
28	- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
29	- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:
30	
31	      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
32	      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB
33	
34	  If your brief gives another session line, use it.
35	
36	## Pushing
37	
38	Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.
39	
40	- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
41	- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
42	  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
43	  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
44	  3. If it lists only your commits, push three times, in this order:
45	
46	         git push origin main
47	         git push origin main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8
48	         git push origin main:blinded-fable
49	
50	     The third push keeps `blinded-fable` current. If the container is lost, the platform rebuilds it from that branch.
51	- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
52	- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and say so in your report.

(* AnyList's ||, addLeft and addRight, and the list comprehension, give a list whose element type is the join of its elements' types. *)
component AnyListElementTypeWalk
import List.{...}
export Executable

kinds(l: Any): String =
    "ZZ32:" instanceOf[\List[\ZZ32\]\](l) " Number:" instanceOf[\List[\Number\]\](l) " Object:" instanceOf[\List[\Object\]\](l)

run(): () = do
    a = <|[\ZZ32\] 1, 2|>
    c = a || <|[\String\] "x"|>
    assert(kinds(c), "ZZ32:false Number:false Object:true", "|| of a list of ZZ32 and a list of String")
    assert(|c|, 3, "|| keeps every element")
    d = a.addLeft("y")
    assert(kinds(d), "ZZ32:false Number:false Object:true", "addLeft of a String to a list of ZZ32")
    e = a.addRight(2.5)
    assert(kinds(e), "ZZ32:false Number:true Object:false", "addRight of an RR64 to a list of ZZ32")
    f = a || <|[\ZZ32\] 3|>
    assert(kinds(f), "ZZ32:true Number:false Object:false", "|| of two lists of ZZ32")
    g = <|[\RR64\] 1.5|> || a
    assert(kinds(g), "ZZ32:false Number:true Object:false", "|| of a list of RR64 and a list of ZZ32")
    q = (<|[\ZZ32\] 1|>.addLeft("z")).addRight(3)
    assert(kinds(q), "ZZ32:false Number:false Object:true", "addLeft then addRight")
    assert(|q|, 3, "addLeft then addRight keep every element")
    k: List[\ZZ32\] = <| 2 x | x <- 0#3 |>
    assert(kinds(k), "ZZ32:true Number:false Object:false", "a comprehension at its declared type")
    o = <| (if x = 0 then 1 else 2.5 end) | x <- 0#2 |>
    assert(kinds(o), "ZZ32:false Number:true Object:false", "a comprehension at the join of its elements")
    p = <|[\ZZ32\] x | x <- 0#0 |>
    assert(kinds(p), "ZZ32:true Number:false Object:false", "an empty comprehension at its written type")
    r = <|[\ZZ32\] x | x <- 0#2, x > 0 |>
    assert(kinds(r), "ZZ32:true Number:false Object:false", "a filtered comprehension at its written type")
  end

end

The team's comment AnyList comprises List[\E\] where [\E\] becomes live
(P-151). The disambiguator puts a trait's where-bound type variables in
scope in its comprises clause, self type, parameters, where clause and
members, not its extends clause. The checker opens a type where-clause
variable of a comprises clause at a call as it opens a size: a fresh name,
bounded by its binding's bounds at the trait's arguments and kept in a
registry that every kind environment reads; a comprising trait reached as
a parent is not opened. Walk binds a type where-clause variable as a
symbolic type at load, and its comprises check at load reads it as a
variable that stands for any type. AnyList's addLeft and addRight become
singleton(e) || self and self || singleton(e), the private addL and addR
are removed, and the list comprehension's unwrap casts its collection to
CovariantCollection[\T\]. Edits the original tree: TypeDisambiguator.java,
BuildEnvironments.java, KindEnv.scala, TypeAnalyzer.scala, List.fsi and
List.fss.

# error table, the total and the crash line that follows it.
#
# Why it exists: POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-21, "the library route" - one library, the
# interpreter's, becomes the library the compiler checks - and step 1 of
# coordinator/library-route-judgement.md, which makes the distance to that goal a
# permanent gate stage rather than a one-off script. A change in the count is reported, not red (checker-gate-review.md).
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched:
# javac output and the checker's caches go to the scratch directory (default: $TMPDIR
# or /tmp), and the caches are given to the JVM as -Dfortress.caches, honoured through
# ProjectProperties.java:261-269,283, so default_repository/ is never read or written.
# Exit 0 if the table was produced, 1 if it could not be. 20 s in the main tree,
# measured 2026-09-22; it needs no library rebuild and no warm cache.
#
# The two sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-22 from
# explorations/perf-probes/prelude/, so that the gate does not depend on a probe
# directory: WorldFlip.java (Shell.useInterpreterLibraries() plus
# PhaseOrder.compilerPhaseOrder, both public, which is the world switch without an edit
# to a tracked file) and shadow-src/.../StaticChecker.java, a copy of
# ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java with three
# instrumentation points added: it names each compilation unit it checks and prints that
# unit's error count, and it catches the OverloadingChecker crash instead of dying on it.
# It is put AHEAD of ProjectFortress/build on the classpath, the technique of
# perf-probes/prelude/run-all.sh:33-35. A copy of a tracked source goes stale silently,
# so the checksum of the tracked one is recorded here and the table's "#shadow" line
# says whether it still matches.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false, read
# at OverloadingChecker.scala:77), since 2026-09-27 (climb batch 7). The memo is keyed on
# declaration pairs and hides 27 to 35 errors depending on the build order once an api's
# overloading check runs (perf-probes/nat/triage.md section 1; FACTS.md, "The hidden
# layer, classified"); with it off every build gives one count. The table's "#cache"
# row says so. On the tree of 2026-09-27 the count is 62 with the memo on and off,
# because the FortressLibrary api stops before its overloading check.
set -u

STOCK_SHA=16e6e11df9341a67038b7d7cc9f0d7bb5e5a6149019f09e92545a8b646363a0b   # ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java, 2026-09-22

OUT=${1:-}
if [ -z "$OUT" ] ; then echo "usage: $0 <out-file> [scratch-dir]" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) OUT="$PWD/$OUT" ;; esac
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:-$PWD}
D="$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count"
TARGET=Library/FortressLibrary.fss
SCRATCH=${2:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/checker-count.$$}
STOCK=$FH/ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java
OVERLOAD_CACHE=false     # the overloading checker's memo, off: see the header

mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
if [ -z "$CP" ] ; then echo "checker-count: no classpath from bin/fortress_classpath" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi

**Questions for the curator (decisions not taken).**
- Q1: land the walker split as its own rung ahead of row 680's line, or in the same rung?
- Q2: pursue the solver's re-normalization of meets (§2.3), about 95 % of what remains?
  - Ways: a memo of normalized meets shared across analyzers; fewer reductions in `Formula.and`'s fold.
- Q3: make AST hashing independent of identity hashes (row 488)? That would change iteration orders, and so
  message text, once.

**Commands worked out.**
- **JFR, read without the text dump.** A single-file Java program over `jdk.jfr.consumer.RecordingFile`
  aggregates `jdk.ExecutionSample` within an epoch window, by self, inclusive, callers or callees. A frame's
  `getType()` (Interpreted, JIT compiled, Inlined) shows which methods the JVM never compiled.
- **Methods over the limit:** a `java.lang.classfile` scan of `ProjectFortress/build` for `Code` attributes
  longer than 8,000 bytes.
- **The AST generators by hand, in scratch:**
  1. `javac -cp <scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:ProjectFortress/third_party/astgen/astgen.jar -d <dir>/build ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/astgen/*.java`.
  2. Copy `Fortress.ast` into `<dir>/astgen`.
  3. From there, `java -cp <dir>/build:<scala jars>:ProjectFortress/build:astgen.jar edu.rice.cs.astgen.ASTGen Fortress.ast`. The `.ast` file's `customClassPath ../build` finds the generators.
- **A huge method's compile attempts:** `-XX:-DontCompileHugeMethods -XX:+PrintCompilation`.
- **Moving the identity-hash sequence:** a driver copy that calls `new Object().hashCode()` N times before
  the phases.

# 2. run the compiler phase order over the interpreter's library under a private cache
( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 10 900 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches="$SCRATCH/caches" \

    tail -20 "$SCRATCH/run.txt" >&2 ; exit 1
fi

#!/bin/bash
# The gate's distance stage: the compiled checker over the whole interpreter library, the
# twelve prelude apis and their twelve components, every stage of every unit run whatever
# the earlier stages reported, so that nothing hides behind an early return; one table.
#
# Why it exists: Pavol's answer 11 (POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-26): the full measurement of the
# distance to the switch-over "becomes a report-only stage of phase 3's gates, whose job is
# driving it down". The checker-count stage beside it (../checker-count/run.sh) sees only
# the errors before each api's early return, 62 of about 1,740 on 2026-09-27.
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir] [setting]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched: the
# shadow sources and classes, the driver, the checker's caches (-Dfortress.caches) and the
# JVM's temporary directory (so Rats! leaves nothing in /tmp) go to the scratch directory
# (default: $TMPDIR or /tmp), and the caches are deleted at the end. It never removes
# /tmp/fortress*rats, which other runs on the machine use. Exit 0 if the table was
# produced, 1 if it could not be. One JVM, -Xmx4g, one busy core: 789 s on the idle 4-CPU
# container on 2026-09-27, 14 to 24 minutes under load 7 to 18 (switch-over-distance-flat.md
# section 5); the table's #seconds and #machine rows say what each run took and where.
#
# The setting: "any" by default, the compiled path with the implicit bound Any
# (DistanceMulti's -setting any: the extends-Object pre-desugaring off, as walk's, and the
# compiled-expression desugaring on, as the compile path's). Answer 11 names the compile
# path's setting; batch 7's question 1, answered (a) on 2026-09-27 (POSITIONS.md, the
# numerics plans), bounds an unbounded type parameter by Any, and under it the switch-over
# takes that bound for the compiled path (CLIMB-BATCH-7.md section 1, Q1), so the 372
# "bound Object" errors of the plain compile setting are the setting's, not the library's
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md sections 2.7 and 5: "under (a) the stage runs stage-any").
# On the tree of 2026-09-27 it differs from walk's setting by the compiled-expression
# desugaring's 12 abstract-method errors on bodyless functions, one export error and the
# variance checker's crash on Stream: 1,746 to 1,747 against 1,737 to 1,738 (FACTS.md,
# "The true distance to the switch-over"). The third argument, walk or compile, runs
# another setting, for a comparison with the measurements on file; the gate never passes it.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false), as in
# every run of the measurement: keyed on declaration pairs, it hides 27 to 35 errors
# depending on the build order (FACTS.md, "The overloading checker's memo hides errors
# by build order, so every count runs with it off ...").
#
# The sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-27, so that the gate does not
# depend on a probe directory, as the checker-count stage's were: DistanceMulti.java from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat/ (35ef70584); shadow-patch.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen/ (e5d8cdbd2); add-patch.py and errors.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/ (a7e3df9ad, 14d2f9839); classify.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage/ (e17a9badc); all unchanged but classify.py, which since
# row 577 finds the library places that name three of its classes by their declarations in
# the tree's sources ($FH, passed to table.py), not by line ranges. table.py is new: it

17:## Changing the text: the revision form
43:## Building it
54:## When the text and an implementation disagree
60:## Citing it

1	# The specification
2	
3	Three folders hold the team's specification:
4	
5	- `Specification/` is the team's text, as the revival revises it. It says what the language means, except where a decision of the curator says otherwise.
6	- `Specification-1.0-frozen/` is the unrevised copy. Cite it as "the Working Draft of February 2011". Only `fortress.1.0.pdf` in it is the 1.0 release. Leave this copy unchanged.
7	- `Documentation/Specification/` is the team's later restart, which they did not finish. If its Types chapter, `Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick`, covers a topic, cite it beside `Specification/` as the designers' later word.
8	
9	Appendix I, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, records the changes to the text. Its revival section has one entry for each change that the revival made.
10	
11	A draft build prints the team's `\note{}` boxes, and a release build hides them. Many say that a feature was not built, for example "Reduction variables are not yet supported." Before you record a missing feature as a gap, grep the notes of its chapter: `grep -n '\\note{' Specification/<file>.tex`.
12	
13	The api listings of the library part are generated from the library's `.fsi` files when the specification is built (`Specification/library/apis/`, not in the tree). A listing shows the library itself, so it cannot justify a change of the library. Cite the `.fsi` file.
14	
15	To weigh the specification against the team's later texts, or to find the designers' reason for a rule, read `exploring.md`, "Weighing the sources".
16	
17	## Changing the text: the revision form
18	
19	Every change of the text has the four parts below, so that no disagreement between the text and an implementation stays hidden.
20	
21	1. An entry in the revival section of Appendix I: a `\subsection` with a `\seclabel`. The entry gives:
22	   - the affected sections, the change, its rationale and its effect. The effect names each departure: each way in which walk or the compiled path does not do what the new text says, with its ledger row.
23	   - the original text, quoted with its path and line in `Specification-1.0-frozen/`;
24	   - what a reversal to the alternative not taken would need;
25	   - the decision of the curator that it follows (its POSITIONS entry), or the reason that your brief gives.
26	
27	   For the form, print one entry, about 2 KB: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:Specification/appendices/changes.tex#choice of a coercion'`.
28	
29	2. At each changed passage, a callout that prints in every build, unlike a `\note`:
30	
31	       \revision{<label>}{<what changed, in a sentence or two>}
32	
33	   `<label>` is the `\seclabel` of the entry. `Specification/fortress/fortress.tex` defines `\revision`.
34	
35	3. The front matter's one paragraph on the revision, in `Specification/fortress/preamble.tex`. If your change makes it false, correct it.
36	
37	4. The full reasoning, in `decision-record.md` in the folder of your work under `explorations/`: each changed passage, the original and the new text, the reason, and the way back. For the form, print one passage of an earlier record, about 4 KB: `explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh 'doc:explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/decision-record.md#3.3'`.
38	
39	If the revision refuses an example, keep the example in the text, marked "Not allowed", as the specification itself does. If your change contradicts a calculus of Appendix A, keep the calculus's rules and soundness claims. Add a callout to it that says what it predates.
40	
41	Check each changed sentence of `Specification/` or `Documentation/` against the curator's decisions. If it says what walk or the compiled path does, run a program that shows it.
42	
43	## Building it
44	
45	To check your LaTeX, build the specification in a built tree, after the setup lines. It takes about 90 s, so start it detached (`session.md`, "Long commands"):
46	
47	    nohup bash -c '( cd Specification/fortress && ./ant genSource && ./ant tex ) > tmp/spec.txt 2>&1; echo EXIT=$? >> tmp/spec.txt' >/dev/null 2>&1 &
48	
49	- Both commands must end in `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, and `grep -c 'Reference .* undefined\|multiply defined\|Undefined control sequence' Specification/fortress/fortress.log` must print 0.
50	- If `pdflatex` is missing, install the packages of the `PKGS` line of `explorations/experiment/setup.sh` with `apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y`.
51	- The build writes only ignored files, its log among them, which can reach 400 MB. Remove them afterwards: `git clean -fXq -- Specification`.
52	- Update `Specification/fortress.pdf` only if your brief asks for it: copy `Specification/fortress/fortress.pdf` over it.
53	
54	## When the text and an implementation disagree
55	
56	- If a decision of the curator says which side is correct, the other side is wrong. If the wrong side is in your area, change it to agree. If not, record the departure as `tests-writing.md`, "How a defect is recorded", says.
57	- If no decision says so, the disagreement is a conflict. Switch to exploring (`exploring.md`).
58	- If the passage has an Appendix I entry, name the departure or the conflict in the entry's effect, with its ledger row. Then the text claims no more than holds.
59	
60	## Citing it
61	
62	- If your change renames or removes a section that a test names, update that citation in the same commit.
63	- Inside the text, cite a section with `\secref{label}`.

64:- P-149 **An object that inherits an abstract functional method from one trait and its body from a sibling trait, and declares none of its own, is refused (Q1).** So `object O extends { A, B }`, with `pick(self)` abstract in `A` and given a body in `B`, must declare its own `pick`, as the specification's text and the type group's Welterweight calculus require and as walk already does; an abstract and a concrete declaration of one method in one trait are refused too. Why: the revival honors the designers' intent and does not change Fortress's nature for a convenience; other languages are consulted only to reconcile a conflict between earlier and later designers' choices, and here there is none. No library type uses the shape. Built by climb batch 16's rung K (`c23b85fdc`): rows 572, 727 and 734 closed.
65:- P-151 **Only the `where` forms the team wrote down are built.** A trait that extends another under a `where` condition is that type only where the condition holds, and its members are checked under the condition; a method's `where` condition bounds its static parameters; and the team's comment `AnyList comprises List[\E\] where [\E\]` becomes live. `SUM`'s fusion with `MAX` and `MIN` stays, the team's commented generic `distribute` measured for its two type errors; the rest of `AnyList` moves into `List`. Why: build what the team left, and add nothing it did not. Still to build: the batch after climb batch 16.
111:- P-150 **No resident compiler is built.** One warm JVM that serves many Fortress commands, as Scala 2's `fsc` did, would save at most 1.8 % of the workers' time, so the speed work goes to the checker itself (P-148). It is weighed again only if that share grows much, for example once programs are compiled often after the switch-over.

and the corresponding instantiations of the generic type in this set'', one
generic type $G$ determining another $G'$ ``if every parameter of $G'$ is a
parameter of $G$''
(\nolinkurl{Documentation/Specification/Prose/Language/types.tick}, lines
277--283 and 384--390, in the revival's repository).
Welterweight Fortress, the calculus of the type group's paper of 2012
(Chase, Hilburn, Luchangco, Naden, Ryu, Steele, and Tristan, ``Dynamic
Dispatch and Type Inference Semipredicates''), reads it at the level of
values: ``no value can belong to the trait unless it also belongs to one of
the comprised types''; its rule for a trait declaration asks nothing of the
traits that extend a trait with such a clause
(\nolinkurl{Papers/Welterweight/grammar.tick}, lines 21--22;
\nolinkurl{Papers/Welterweight/fig-wellformeddecls.tick}, lines 38--62).
The draft note restated the rule of the compiled type checker of 2009,
under which \library\ could not close their marker of the integer types as
the team meant to: \TYP{AnyIntegral} lists the five integer types, and the
parameterized trait \EXP{\TYP{Integral}\llbracket{}I\rrbracket}, which each
of them extends at itself, stands between them unlisted, as the team's
comment on the declaration records (``not yet: comprises
\EXP{\TYP{Integral}\llbracket{}I\rrbracket} where
\EXP{\llbracket{}I\rrbracket}'', \nolinkurl{Library/FortressLibrary.fsi},
line 434).
\TYP{Integral} has a static parameter that \TYP{AnyIntegral} does not have,
so it can be listed only at particular static arguments, and every value of it is a value of one of the five.
The full reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-spec-comprises/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
The amendment follows the revival's default for the third question of its
array design, a size known only at run time, built on 9~October 2026 and
listed for the curator's review.

1446	has no static parameters, is still not allowed.
1447	The compiled type checker enforces the requirement on a trait with static
1448	parameters over the declarations and object expressions it sees: a trait or object declared in
1449	another component, below such a trait and a subtype of no listed type, is
1450	not refused (row~487 of the revival's gap ledger). It compares the declarations it sees by their names: for a parameterized \VAR{T} its verdict can depend on how an extender spells its static parameters, and a trait or object that extends a trait of the same simple name in another API counts as an extender (rows~489 and~490).
1451	It refuses an object expression that extends a trait with a \KWD{comprises}
1452	clause, explicitly or through the traits it extends, and is a subtype of no
1453	listed type, as the requirement on the trait's extenders together demands of
1454	it, an object expression having neither static parameters nor a clause of its
1455	own; before 3~October 2026 it read no object expression against a clause
1456	(row~597).
1457	The interpreter checks at load the traits and objects that explicitly extend a
1458	trait with a \KWD{comprises} clause declared in the component it executes, and
1459	refuses one that is neither a subtype of a listed type nor another of the
1460	extenders that \secref{trait-decls} allows.
1461	It does not yet check a clause declared in another component, of the program
1462	or of \library\ (rows~22, 487, 551, 595 and~596), an object expression that
1463	extends such a trait (row~597), or that each listed type extends \VAR{T}
1464	(row~598).
1465	By the amendment, the compiled type checker reads a \KWD{nat} or \KWD{int}
1466	\KWD{where}-clause variable as a size, reads a listed type at every value of
1467	such a variable when it checks the traits and objects that extend \VAR{T}, and
1468	opens an argument as the new sentence of \secref{natparams} says, so that the
1469	value of \VAR{reflect} in \library\ is accepted where an
1470	\EXP{N\llbracket{}n\rrbracket} is expected; it refuses an opened size that
1471	reaches a type naming another size, and gives two values opened in one call
1472	two sizes, so it refuses a call that needs them equal where the interpreter
1473	runs it when they are.
1474	It reads a declaration whose parameter type is such a trait and a declaration
1475	with a \KWD{nat} parameter whose parameter type is the listed type at it as
1476	applicable to the same calls, and refuses the pair as duplicates, where the
1477	interpreter runs it and calls the second; the text does not say whether the
1478	opening counts for the rules of \secref{overloading-static-params}
1479	(row~682 of the revival's gap ledger).
1480	It does not yet open a type \KWD{where}-clause variable, as in
1481	\TYP{List}'s commented clause (row~636), and the code generator does not yet
1482	compile a trait with a \KWD{where} clause or read a size off an argument at a
1483	call (row~307).
1484	The interpreter binds such a variable as a size when it loads the trait, reads
1485	a listed type at every value of it in its check at load, and binds the size of
1486	an argument when it dispatches.
1487	\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/traits.tex},
1488	lines 230--241, a draft note:
1489	\begin{quote}
1490	If a trait declaration of \VAR{T} includes a \KWD{comprises} clause
1491	then the traits listed in its \KWD{comprises} clause
1492	are exactly the traits that immediately extend \VAR{T}
1493	and they must explicitly extend \VAR{T}
1494	(i.e., list \VAR{T} in their \KWD{extends} clause).
1495	If the \KWD{comprises} clause of a trait \VAR{T} includes ``\EXP{\ldots}''
1496	(and must therefore be in an API),
1497	then in a component exporting the enclosing API,
1498	other traits may explicitly extend \VAR{T},
1499	but these traits may not be declared or imported by the API

1501	\end{quote}
